questiontext.text:
Question ID: ALG2_U05_Pretest_Q01

MLA Standard: MLA.A2.SYS.1; MLA.A2.SYS.2

Solve the system y=x+3 and y=7.

feedback.text: Correct. Substitute y=7 into 7=x+3, then subtract 3.
This uses the constant from the equation, not the solution.
This is the y-value, not the x-value.
This adds 7 and 3 instead of solving.

questiontext.text:
Question ID: ALG2_U05_Pretest_Q02

MLA Standard: MLA.A2.SYS.3

Which point satisfies both y>2x and y<9?

feedback.text: This gives y=8, but 8 is not greater than 2(4)=8.
Correct. 7>6 and 7<9, so both inequalities are true.
This is greater than 9, so it fails the second inequality.
This is less than 2(2)=4, so it fails the first inequality.

questiontext.text:
Question ID: ALG2_U05_Pretest_Q03

MLA Standard: MLA.A2.SYS.4

A line and a parabola intersect at (-1,2) and (3,6). What are the system solutions?

feedback.text: These are y-values, not complete system solution inputs.
This misses the second intersection.
Correct. System solutions are the points that satisfy both equations.
Two intersection points are given, so the system has solutions.

questiontext.text:
Question ID: ALG2_U05_Pretest_Q04

MLA Standard: MLA.A2.FN.4; MLA.A2.FN.5; MLA.A2.FN.6

How does y=(x-4)²+1 transform y=x²?

feedback.text: The inside sign is interpreted oppositely.
The outside constant is positive, so the shift is up.
This switches the horizontal and vertical shifts.
Correct. x-4 shifts right 4, and +1 shifts up 1.

questiontext.text:
Question ID: ALG2_U05_Pretest_Q05

MLA Standard: MLA.A2.FN.7; MLA.A2.FN.8

If f(x)=x+2 and g(x)=5x, what is f(g(2))?

feedback.text: Correct. g(2)=10, then f(10)=12.
This stops after evaluating g(2).
This applies f to 5 instead of applying g to 2 first.
This multiplies after adding instead of composing.

questiontext.text:
Question ID: ALG2_U05_Pretest_Q06

MLA Standard: MLA.A2.FN.7; MLA.A2.FN.8

For (f/g)(x), which inputs must be excluded?

feedback.text: A zero numerator is allowed in a quotient.
Correct. The denominator cannot equal zero.
Negative values are not automatically excluded.
Only inputs that make the denominator zero are excluded.

questiontext.text:
Question ID: ALG2_U05_Pretest_Q07

MLA Standard: MLA.A2.FN.9; MLA.A2.FN.10

Find the inverse of f(x)=2x-6.

feedback.text: This does not reverse the order of operations.
The sign should change when undoing -6.
Correct. Add 6 first, then divide by 2.
Inverse function notation does not mean reciprocal.

questiontext.text:
Question ID: ALG2_U05_Pretest_Q08

MLA Standard: MLA.A2.FN.9; MLA.A2.FN.10

Which check verifies that f and g are inverse functions?

feedback.text: This checks additive opposites, not inverse functions.
This checks reciprocals in special cases, not inverse functions.
Inverse functions do not usually have identical rules.
Correct. Both compositions must return the original input.

questiontext.text:
Question ID: ALG2_U05_Pretest_Q09

MLA Standard: MLA.A2.FN.3; MLA.A2.FN.11; MLA.A2.FN.12

What is the average rate of change from (1,5) to (4,17)?

feedback.text: This is the change in input, not the rate.
This is the change in output before dividing.
This adds the output values.

questiontext.text:
Question ID: ALG2_U05_Pretest_Q10

MLA Standard: MLA.A2.FN.3; MLA.A2.FN.11; MLA.A2.FN.12

A context gives possible times t=-3 and t=8. Which value is viable?

feedback.text: Negative time before the starting point is not viable.
Correct. The positive time value is viable in this context.
The negative time value violates the context.
The positive time value is viable.
